chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir and Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from al-Ala' ibn Razin al-Qalla', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Qa'im (May Allah hasten his reappearance): when he rises, with which manner of conduct does he proceed among the people? He said: 'With the manner of conduct with which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) proceeded, until he makes Islam manifest.' I said: 'And what was the manner of conduct of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said: 'He abolished what existed in the era of Ignorance (al-Jahiliyyah) and faced the people with justice. And so too is the Qa'im (peace be upon him) when he rises: he abolishes what existed during the truce (al-Hudna) that was in the hands of the people, and faces them with justice.'

key_terms.الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: The Era of Ignorance (pre-Islamic period of ignorance and injustice)
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Riser, a title for the Mahdi
key_terms.الْهُدْنَةِ: The Truce (referring to the period of temporary peace or status quo before the Mahdi's rise)
key_terms.عَجَّلَ اللَّهُ فَرَجَهُ: May Allah hasten his reappearance (a common honorific for the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What is the political methodology of the Mahdi (al-Qa'im) when he rises?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the political methodology of the Mahdi (AS), emphasizing that his rise will mirror the Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) transition from the *Jahiliyyah* to divine justice. The term *al-Hudnah* (truce) is interpreted by Shia scholars as the period of political quietism or the status quo ante, which the Mahdi will nullify to establish a universal government based on equity, thereby fulfilling the prophetic legacy of abolishing pre-Islamic customs and institutionalizing justice.
